images.title: Which number is greater?
images.purpose: Show 8,965 and 21,304 one above the other in the place value chart so the number of digits can be compared.
images.composition: A chart with a number column and two number rows, a digit count beside each row and the comparison written large below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Centre: a table with 6 columns and 3 rows: a left column about 240 px wide for the whole number, then 5 equal columns (about 150 px each). Header row: the left cell is empty, then TTh, Th, H, T, O in white bold letters on blue #0072B2 cells. Row 1: the left cell holds 8,965 in bold dark numerals (60 px); then the TTh cell is empty with a dashed grey #6B7280 outline, and the cells Th, H, T, O hold 8, 9, 6, 5. Row 2: the left cell holds 21,304 in bold dark numerals (60 px); then the cells TTh, Th, H, T, O hold 2, 1, 3, 0, 4. The 2 in the TTh cell has a reddish purple #CC79A7 fill. All digits in the cells are large bold dark numerals (80 px). A thin grey #6B7280 double-headed vertical arrow sits between the two number cells in the left column. To the right of the chart, aligned with each row, a small dark tag: 4 digits beside row 1 and 5 digits beside row 2 (40 px). Bottom centre: 21,304 > 8,965 in very large bold dark numerals (100 px), with the > sign in reddish purple #CC79A7.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Count the digits first: the number with more digits is greater, even if its first digit is smaller.
images.description: A place value chart with 8,965 in the first row (TTh empty) and 21,304 in the second row, tagged 4 digits and 5 digits, with 21,304 > 8,965 written below.
images.context: Concept image for Which number is greater? It follows the figure in your maths book of two numbers one above the other in the chart and uses the first part of the video's own example, 8,965 and 21,304.
images.teaching_notes: Students often think 8 is greater than 2, so 8,965 is greater. Show that the 2 sits in TTh and is worth 20,000, while the 8 is only 8,000. The empty TTh cell in row 1 shows that 8,965 has no ten thousands.

image_decisions.why: The two numbers stacked in one chart make the extra TTh digit visible, which decides the comparison.
